newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi sees 1st half PSBR 25 trillion lire.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi sees 1st half PSBR 25 trillion lire.

text.p: Treasury Minster Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Tuesday he expected Italy's public sector borrowing requirement in the first half of 1997 to be 25 trillion lire.
Ciampi told the Senate (upper house) that he was confident Italy would reach the three percent deficit-to-Gross Domestic Product goal for entry into Europe's planned single currency.
"First half data is comforting. It should close with a public sector borrowing requirement of around 25 trillion lire, less than half the level of 53.7 trillion in the first half of 1996," he said.
Budget Undersecretary Giorgio Macciotta said earlier that the government hoped for a budget surplus of 30 trillion lire in June, compared with a surplus of 25 trillion lire in June 1996.
A budget surplus in the order of 30 trillion lire would slash Italy's first half PSBR to around 25 trillion lire.
